reproduction.result: Experiment 003's configuration, replayed on this tree, reproduces every published per-episode row and summary it published: the lookahead side 912.8 mean lines and 2,822,959.9 mean score, the tetris side 349.5 mean lines and 567,266.2 mean score, which are the numbers the acceptance criteria name

conclusion: The bounded well plan meets all three acceptance thresholds on Experiment 003's identical ten seeds: a Tetris line rate of 0.03871 against the required 0.011445 (240 Tetris lines in 6200 lines, 3.38x the Experiment 003 baseline's rate), 620.0 mean lines against more than 349.5 (1.77x) and 1665036.0 mean score against more than 567,266.2 (2.94x), with no episode stopped at the frame cap. Two changes to the objective are what move them, and the measurements are attributed to both rather than to the plan alone. The plan is a designated well column, an explicit stack-height budget, a reserve measured as the rows a vertical I would complete above the column's topmost filled cell, and a spend-or-abandon rule at a self-tracked I-drought bound. Beside it, the composition scores the current placement's whole plan value, where Experiment 003 adds only that placement's clear term to the preview's value: the objective_mechanism block derives one reachable board per phase on which the two compositions select different placements, so the evaluation does not rest on the claim that the two compose a current placement alike. It does not reach the frozen lookahead agent's survival on the same seeds, so the plan buys Tetris rate with lines rather than adding both, and that trade is the experiment's main limitation. The three thresholds are met by the re-measurement taken after the plan's height accounting was corrected, whose per-episode rows and metrics are identical to the superseded run's, so the verdict is the same measurement under corrected code rather than a revised one.

limitations: The plan agent was measured only on classic_ntsc_extended, endless, start level 18, height 0, the settings Experiments 002 and 003 used. Nothing here measures another ruleset, level or mode, and no live-desktop game or whole-game mode was run.

The plan's constants were fixed on a development seed set (odd seeds 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 15, 17, 19, 21, 23) that excludes the ten evaluation seeds. That is development, not evaluation: the numbers above are the first measurement of these constants on the evaluation seeds, and notes.md states the development.

The plan's advantage over Experiment 003's agent is bounded and specific: it is a one-piece, straight-drop, commit-per-piece policy. It does not search, it does not know a future piece beyond the visible preview, and it cannot repair a covered cell. The reserve it holds is therefore often partial: only 60 of its 15857 placements were four-line clears. A reserve is only ever earned through the field: well_reserve counts the rows a vertical I would complete above the designated column's topmost filled cell, so a well column already filled low down still holds a reserve for the rows above it and the count is not restricted to a column open to the floor. The objective_mechanism block derives a board of exactly that shape -- the designated column occupied with well_reserve 1 -- rather than stating the rule in prose.

The measurement is not attributable to the explicit plan alone. The objective also composes a current placement differently from Experiment 003's: it adds plan_value for that placement -- the field terms, the reserve and the overflow in BUILD, and the entire frozen feature_score in SPEND -- where Experiment 003's tetris_choice adds only clear_term for it and scores the preview's board by its own value. The objective_mechanism block derives one reachable board per phase on which the two compositions select different placements, so the claim that they compose a current placement alike is not relied on anywhere. What was not measured is a run of Experiment 003's composition under this plan's phase, budget and drought memory: that comparison, and any attribution of the measured lines and score between the plan and the composition, is left to a later experiment.

The plan agent clears fewer lines and scores less than the frozen lookahead agent it runs beside on the same seeds (620.0 against 912.8 mean lines, 1,665,036 against 2,822,959.9 mean score). It preserves the Tetris rate at a cost in survival; the aspirational comparison is reported, not met.

All ten plan games topped out, so the ten-seed means are top-out outcomes rather than frame-capped games; one lookahead game stopped at the 200000-frame cap instead. The per-episode rows are retained so both cases are visible.

The declared-objective identity covers the code that selects which implementation is built, as well as the module that builds the agent whose placements a record replays. That is why the plan agent is declared in its objective module (block_stack_ai.wellplan) and built by the runner's per-agent dispatch (runner.DECLARED_OBJECTIVES, runner.build_agent) instead of being added to the shared agent factory (block_stack_ai.agents): the factory's source is byte-identical to the branch base, so the frozen Experiment 003 record's identity still equals this tree's, while a plan record's identity covers the dispatch module (block_stack_ai.runner) and so catches a change to it. The Tetris identity stays the five modules its version-6 writer recorded, because Experiment 003's retained capture and the frozen fixture are compared against exactly that mapping: a change to runner.build_agent that kept a Tetris record replaying would still go unreported. That residual -- and the reason the wider shape cannot be had, since a new format version would move the constant Experiment 003's retained record_format_versions prose derives 'current suite' from -- is re-derived by check-record in the `dispatcher_coverage` block rather than asserted here. `check-record` derives both digests -- the factory's and the dispatcher's -- from those modules' own bytes rather than restating them. See objective_record.shared_module_caveat.

This file is a distilled record, not the full run record: the evaluation's own run.json is about 17 MB of ignored, disposable output holding one input mask per logical frame. The evidence is therefore re-derived from the code rather than replayed from stored inputs -- retained_replay re-plays the retained configuration and compares every outcome and metric -- and the temporary record the predeclaration cites is named here for as long as this checkout keeps it.

Two declared-objective agents cannot be configured in one suite: a version-6 record carries one objective section. A comparison of tetris and tetris_plan in one run is therefore not expressible, and this experiment compares the plan against Experiment 003's retained rows and against a re-run of Experiment 003's own configuration instead.

The plan's height accounting was corrected after the first publication: a column whose cells rest in the engine's two hidden rows is stack height (22 on the plan's scale, against the frozen visible-field measure of 0) rather than an empty column, so the budget, the SPEND transition and the overflow term read that state correctly. The retained evaluation was re-measured under the corrected code and its per-episode rows and metrics are identical, because no episode of the ten reached that state; the corrected reading is derived in objective_mechanism.hidden_rows_are_stack_height and reached on the engine itself by tests/test_integration.py::test_the_plan_reads_a_native_hidden_stack_as_over_its_budget.

objective_record.compatibility: The section's name, shape and format version are unchanged, so records written before it keep verifying: a version-2 suite carries none, a version-4 suite carries the objective without the identity, a version-5 suite's identity stops at what the objective's own code reaches, and a version-6 suite carries the identity with the agent wrapper. Which version's requirements apply is not the record's to choose: the writer that first made an agent configurable is a property of that agent (runner.DECLARED_OBJECTIVES[...].introduced_in), so a record that configures the plan agent below version 6 -- a combination no writer ever emitted, because the plan agent was introduced by the version-6 writer -- is reported as an edit before any section is compared, and it cannot be relabelled out of the objective, the identity or the dispatcher digest. Above that floor the version's own writer's requirements hold: a version-4 or version-5 record whose configuration selects a declared-objective agent must carry the section, and an identity it does carry is compared in every case, while a version-2 record of the Tetris agent legitimately carries neither.
objective_record.generalization: The runner no longer hard-wires the declared-objective section to block_stack_ai.tetris. It resolves it through runner.DECLARED_OBJECTIVES, a registry keyed by agent name, so the section names the objective of whichever agent the configuration selects: the module that declares it, the weights that module publishes and the identity of the modules its choices run through. The identity walk is seeded from that agent's objective module and from the module that selects which implementation is built -- the shared agent factory for an agent it defines, or runner's dispatch (runner.DECLARED_OBJECTIVES, runner.build_agent) for an agent whose objective module owns it -- and it excludes the other declared objectives, because the factory imports them all: without the exclusion a well-plan record would be invalidated by an edit to the Tetris objective, whose code no plan choice runs. The Tetris objective's own covered set is therefore unchanged by this experiment, and the plan's covers the dispatch module as well. A record carries one such section, so parse_suite_config refuses a configuration that names two declared-objective agents.
objective_record.shared_module_caveat: The identity covers block_stack_ai.agents, the module that defines the agent factory, because Experiment 003's own repair added it there so that a wrapper change preserving the replayed choices could not be certified. That module is shared by every agent the factory dispatches, so this experiment did not add the plan agent to it: the plan agent is declared in block_stack_ai.wellplan and built by the runner's per-agent dispatch (runner.DECLARED_OBJECTIVES, runner.build_agent). The shared factory's source is therefore byte-identical to the branch base, and its digest is 2b24e1b2... in Experiment 003's capture and in this tree's own capture, run identity and retained result alike. A plan record's identity additionally covers the dispatch module itself, block_stack_ai.runner, whose digest for this tree's bytes is in `sources` beside the factory's: that is the code which decides the plan agent is built by wellplan at all, and a change to it that still replayed the recorded inputs is now reported rather than certified. The Tetris identity keeps the five modules its version-6 writer recorded -- Experiment 003's retained capture and the retained fixture are compared against exactly that mapping -- so the dispatch module is not part of it, and a plan record written before this correction (the previous publication's temporary run) is now reported against the fuller identity instead of verifying under it. The version-6 record written by the frozen Experiment 003-era writer therefore verifies on this tree with only the engine's working-tree warning: `probes/evidence.py check-record` derives both digests from the modules' bytes and compares them with the retained fixture's identity and with this result's own claims, and `tests/test_integration.py::test_a_record_written_by_the_frozen_writer_still_verifies` re-derives the factory's too. What the generalised section preserves is stated and re-derived as well: the record formats keep their dispatch and their optional sections, the frozen objective's module, weights and formula are untouched, and every published row of Experiment 003 reproduces exactly -- item 'baseline'.

predeclared_objective.capture_order: the capture was written at 2026-09-30T02:06:32.477792+00:00, before the cited record's own created_at 2026-09-30T02:06:49.115337+00:00, and the record's own objective identity is the capture's
predeclared_objective.identity_coverage: The capture records the digest of every module the plan's decisions are computed from, the same set the run's own objective.sources enumerates: the declaring module (wellplan), the frozen geometry and board model it imports (heuristic, pieces), Experiment 002's reachable-set enumeration it reuses (pathaware), the agent wrapper that hands it the state and the shared factory class it is built from (agents), the game factory whose create_game builds the state every choice reads (engine), and the module whose dispatch decides the plan agent is built by wellplan at all (runner). Seven modules. The walk is the runner's own, not a hand-listed set; it excludes the sibling Tetris objective, and the one package module it never covers is the provenance recorder itself, which cannot record its own load because it installs the recorder. `check-predeclaration` requires the capture to equal the current modules and the identity the run itself wrote, `check-record` re-derives it from the retained result, and the dispatcher's digest is derived from runner's own bytes and compared with both copies.
predeclared_objective.note: the declared objective -- the module, the modules its decisions are computed from, and the documented weights, plan constants and rationale -- captured from the unmodified tree before the evaluation run; no constant is revised against evaluation outcomes. The constants were fixed on a development seed set that excludes the ten evaluation seeds (odd seeds 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 15, 17, 19, 21, 23); that development is stated in notes.md rather than presented as a pre-existing choice. This capture supersedes three earlier ones, kept beside it: predeclared_objective.pre-height-fix.json, taken before the plan's height accounting was corrected so a column resting in the engine's hidden rows counts as stack height rather than as an empty column; predeclared_objective.pre-dispatch.json, whose identity walked the objective module and the wrapper but not the dispatch that selects the agent; and predeclared_objective.pre-agent-move.json, taken before the agent was moved out of the shared factory. Each was valid for the design it preceded, and `check-record` requires each named superseded capture to exist, to predate this one and to describe a different subject.
